answer: Each identity tends one garden bed, mounts one mirror on a thread, locks an 80-credit bond, and files the thread length, mirror tilt, and noon light. An auditor recomputes the expected reflection from the public garden sun-angle table: tilt and thread length fix the mirror geometry, so an off-table reading burns the bond. The first filing costs 38 credits; the kth costs 38+8(k-1), so the 1000th costs 8030, and 1000 fakes pay 4,034,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-mirror ring fails because one rig serves one bed at noon, and a reused serial burns both bonds. An honest gardener pays 38 once.
